title: Pin the tested Amiga BASIC setup and state its actual requirements
body:
The Blitz getting-started page recommends AmiBlitz3 and an A1200/accelerated A500 with Kickstart 3.0+, but omits the IDE's CPU/RAM/disk/library requirements. Upstream README at 5dd815f880d72c5285b380ef3ddebfa5766d0626 requires a 68020, at least 8 MB RAM, 35 MB disk and its named Workbench/library setup. A machine name alone does not specify those resources. The page also directs readers to Ted and promises all original Blitz BASIC 2 course examples run unchanged, without a named tested release.

Correct `src/content/curriculum/commodore-amiga/blitz/getting-started.mdx` after qualifying one exact runtime route. Distinguish original Blitz BASIC 2 from AmiBlitz3, name the verified IDE/runtime and emulator configuration, and follow its actual launch/compile controls. State requirements for the IDE separately from generated programs. Check AMOS's paired on-ramp against its chosen distribution too; keep source-licence and disk-distribution claims scoped to the actual artefact.

Acceptance: a beginner can reproduce the setup and first greeting using named versions/configuration; retain source-to-execution evidence and working source/download links. Do not infer a runtime failure from this documentation mismatch. No new course structure or dependency is authorised by this issue.

Primary requirements: https://github.com/AmiBlitz/AmiBlitz3/blob/5dd815f880d72c5285b380ef3ddebfa5766d0626/README.md . Parent: stevehill1981/198x#116. Coordinate with the bounded greeting qualification in the audit report.

title: Qualify the Amiga opening lessons’ speed and representation claims
body:
The reviewed AMOS/Blitz openings make workload-free performance and safety claims. Examples include Blitz unit 1's “compiled code runs many times faster” and unit 3's comparison that an interpreted AMOS number uses a “big, safe box for everything”. The mode lesson also generalises its OS trade to every Amiga game. The included sources/captures demonstrate greetings, graphics and one byte wrap; they supply no comparative timing or whole-language range proof.

Review only the two module overviews and first three units of each track. Preserve the concrete edit/run/compile and storage explanations, but replace general rankings with named mechanisms and explicit boundaries. Treat runtime type/range behaviour as a language contract requiring primary documentation and selected execution, and performance as a processor/language/workload measurement. Do not add invented benchmarks or use a historical generalisation as proof.

Acceptance: retain exact before/after claims and primary citations; any comparative measurement names the same task/configuration and preserves correct results. Keep AMOS and Blitz independent peers. Verify the changed prose and representative rendered pages; no broad rewrite.

Parent: stevehill1981/198x#116. Source audit: Code198x/docs `audit/2026-10-amiga-opening/REPORT.md` (pending review).

title: Qualify the first AMOS and Blitz greetings with named runtime identities
body:
The opening source audit confirms six lesson includes and six capture-driver typing payloads match their maintained source. The six capture manifests name only `commodore-amiga-amos` or `commodore-amiga-blitz`; they do not bind a particular CPU, RAM, ROM/OS, editor/compiler release or observed run result. Existing screenshots agree visually with the stated result but do not prove a repeatable source-to-runtime route. The inspected Build Amiga Assembly CI job builds `.asm`; its success is not AMOS/Blitz qualification.

Bound the next execution slice to unit 1 of Meet AMOS and unit 1 of Meet Blitz. Resolve one lawful installed runtime/distribution for each, record exact emulator/machine/ROM/OS/runtime identities and source hashes, enter/load the maintained greeting, run/compile it, observe the greeting, change its words and recover from a deliberate syntax error. Record unavailable media or tools as skipped/unknown. Do not substitute a fabricated transcript, image or host-language simulation.

Acceptance: retain actual source, build/run observations, edited result and negative/error-repair evidence with declared limits. Resolve the paired website setup issue from the same proven route before scaling. No new dependencies or licensed media downloads without normal project approval. Parent: stevehill1981/198x#116; related cross-stack qualification #69 remains separate.
